conflicting_evidence: Same gold annotation resolves to brivaracetam on every other field: CUIPhrase='brivaracetam', CUI='C1699861', and the annotated span text is 'Brivetiracetam-' (a typo of brivaracetam). DrugName is the sole field naming perampanel.
notes: Found in Phase 0 pipeline assumption audit (docs/research/exectv2_pipeline_assumption_audit_2026-07-02.md, 'Drug-lexicon gaps' section) and confirmed on the frozen dev140 corpus in Phase 3. Frozen corpus NOT edited. Effect on scoring: under canonicalize_medication_name the gold clinical_headline key carries name='perampanel' while a model prediction matching the span ('Brivetiracetam'->brivaracetam) keys to name='brivaracetam', so this fact cannot be a true positive regardless of model correctness (mislabels a defensible prediction as FP+FN). Discovered 2026-07-02. Corpus-audit confirmation (2026-07-09): swept all Prescription mentions for DrugName values sharing no text overlap with CUIPhrase/span. 16 candidates found; 15 of 16 are legitimate UK brand-to-generic resolutions (Epilim/Episenta->Sodium Valproate, Lamictal->Lamotrigine, Tegretol->Carbamazepine) and NOT errors. EA0146 remains the only genuine DrugName/CUIPhrase mismatch in the corpus.

conflicting_evidence: Gold mention T2 (offsets 621-651, span 'generlised-tonic-clonic-seizur') is annotated over the sentence 'he gets around 1 generlised tonic clonic seizure in his sleep per month.' Gold's own CUIPhrase/CUI/NumberOfSeizures on this mention are consistent with the sentence (NumberOfSeizures=1), but TimePeriod=Year/NumberOfTimePeriods=2 has no textual basis anywhere near the span -- the sentence says 'per month', not 'per 2 years'. No other sentence in the letter mentions a 2-year cadence for this seizure type.
notes: Found while auditing SF inspection tab false positives. The magnitude-complement dev140 prediction (experiments/exectv2_sf_magnitude_complement_dev140_20260708.jsonl, letter_id=EA0079) reads NumberOfSeizures=1, NumberOfTimePeriods=1, TimePeriod=Month for this exact sentence -- textually correct, and arguably more precise than gold. Effect on scoring: TimePeriod/NumberOfTimePeriods conflict outright (this is NOT the point/range shape-equivalence class of bug fixed the same day -- there is no Lower/Upper duality here, it's a genuine gold value error), so the mention scores as a straight FN(gold)+FP(pred) with no distinguishing signal from a real hallucination. Frozen corpus NOT edited. Corpus-audit confirmation (2026-07-09): swept all 263 SeizureFrequency mentions in the 200-letter gold corpus for this same error class (TimePeriod/NumberOfTimePeriods with no textual rate-marker support in the mention's sentence, on mentions with NumberOfSeizures>0). EA0079 is the ONLY instance. One superficially similar candidate (EA0134 T17, NumberOfSeizures=0, TimePeriod=Year/2 for 'her last seizure was 2 years ago') is NOT an error -- it instances a legitimate, corpus-wide convention (33 other NumberOfSeizures=0 mentions) where TimePeriod/NumberOfTimePeriods encodes seizure-free duration since the last event, which IS textually grounded. See experiments/audit_sf_timeperiod_2026-07-09.py for the detector.

conflicting_evidence: Gold mention T3 (offsets 248-256, span 'seizures') is annotated over 'Last week she had around 10-15 of these seizures over 2 days.' NumberOfTimePeriods=2 is correct (matches '2 days'), but TimePeriod is coded as the lowercase/plural literal 'days' instead of the schema's canonical enum value 'Day' -- the only non-canonical TimePeriod value in the entire corpus (7 Day / 44 Month / 35 Week / 54 Year / 1 days).
notes: Not a content error like EA0079/EA0146 -- the underlying fact (2 seizures over 2 days) is textually correct, this is a closed-vocab casing/pluralization quirk. Already flagged in docs/research/exectv2_data_discoveries_log.md (D14, 2026-06-09/10: 'annotation noise, normalize where safe (days->Day)') and accepted into the closed_vocab (contract/entities.py:233) so gold validates clean, but the recommended normalization was never wired into scoring: canonicalize_attribute_value (scoring/normalize.py) only lowercases DrugName/DoseUnit, and the deterministic/normalizer.py days->Day map applies to model predictions, never to gold. Net effect: a correct model prediction of TimePeriod=Day for this one mention would silently fail to match gold under exact-value scoring. Fixed 2026-07-09 by adding TimePeriod to the day/week/month/year pluralization-normalization in scoring/normalize.py::canonicalize_attribute_value. Single-mention impact (1/263 SF mentions).
